**Definition**: A method for extracting isosurfaces of scalar fields defined on hybrid unstructured grids containing pentahedral elements (square pyramids and right triangular prisms) directly, avoiding the need to subdivide non-tetrahedral cells into tetrahedra or use indirect triangulation methods [S1].

Standard approaches often require converting unstructured data into tetrahedral or hexahedral elements, which can introduce topological errors or computational overhead [S1].

It notes that the proposed method avoids the need for subdivision and processes grids 'directly without subdivision,' implying that the standard/indirect methods do require this conversion (subdivision into tetrahedra or use of hexahedral/tetrahedral specific algorithms like marching cubes/tetrahedra). Furthermore, the evidence mentions constructing look-up tables with 'accurate topological considerations,' implying that standard indirect methods may lack this accuracy or introduce topological issues. Thus, the evidence supports the claim that standard approaches require such conversion and that this process is associated with the need for careful topological handling (avoiding errors) and indirect computation (overhead).
